target_customer: Law firms, especially contingency fee practices, that lose potential clients when calls go unanswered
problem: Law firms miss inbound calls and leads outside office hours, losing revenue. OpenIntake answers calls with AI, captures intake details and books consultations.
business_model: B2B SaaS for law firms (pricing not found)
product_category: Legal tech AI voice receptionist and client intake

founders.name: Yash Sahota
education: Cornell University, B.S. and M.Eng. in computer science (2020)
previous_startups: TripleZip (listed on the YC page, outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: YC page: product security engineer at Slack and consultant at McKinsey.

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents on top of speech and language model APIs plus calendar and CRM integrations are standard engineering for a two person team in early 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Many vendors sell AI receptionists to law firms, and the model layer is shared. Integration with practice management systems can add some switching cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Human and hybrid legal answering services existed and added AI intake chatbots (Answering Legal launched one in July 2025). Other legal intake startups raised seed rounds in 2025 (Caseflood.ai, Superpanel).

market_need_then: Law firms pay for answering services to avoid missing leads, so budget exists. Better voice AI in 2024 to 2025 made automated 24/7 intake plausible.

branding.domain_note: Uses openintake.ai (company site); acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Benefit-led, as in 'AI Legal Intake That Never Misses a Client'

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive and clear but generic, and no press or community evidence about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: OpenIntake is an active two person YC Winter 2025 company with no reported exit, shutdown or layoffs. No priced round beyond aggregator entries was found, and the market is crowded with answering services and AI voice vendors that raised money in 2025. Its prospects depend on law firm distribution and integrations rather than technology.
notes: Funding unverified: Caplight, PitchBook and StartupHub list about $500K from Y Combinator dated January 2025 (accelerator), which is probably YC's standard deal, so no round is recorded. No dated competitor found near the batch (the Answering Legal chatbot launched July 2025, after the batch), so the list is empty.
